blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights AlphaGo Zero as a groundbreaking achievement in AI, demonstrating superhuman performance in Go without any human knowledge or guidance. Unlike its predecessors, AlphaGo Zero learns solely through self-play reinforcement learning, starting from random moves, and achieves superior results in a fraction of the time and computational resources. The paper showcases how AlphaGo Zero rediscovers fundamental Go strategies (like joseki) and even develops novel tactics beyond traditional human knowledge. The key insight is the feasibility of pure reinforcement learning in complex domains, eliminating the need for human data or heuristics. The blog emphasizes the remarkable efficiency of AlphaGo Zero, outperforming AlphaGo Lee in just 36 hours using a single machine with 4 TPUs, compared to AlphaGo Lee's months-long training and distributed setup with 48 TPUs.
